name: Copper Age
description: Turn your first copper into mechanical power and the beginnings of automation.

pages.text: $(bold)Welcome to the Copper Age$()$(br2)Your first Copper Ingot ends the Stone Age, but Copper is not just a stronger crafting material. This age is about learning to work metal, transmit rotational power, process ore mechanically, and gradually replace manual labor with machinery.$(br2)Producing your first Bronze will eventually mark the end of the Copper Age.

pages.title: Primitive Anvil
pages.text: The Primitive Anvil is your first metalworking station. It gives the Primitive Hammer a real job and turns raw ingots into manufactured machine components.

$(bold)1. Work your first Copper$()$(br2)Right-click the Primitive Anvil with a Copper Ingot to place it on the work surface. The ingot is visible on the anvil while you work.$(br2)Strike it four times with the Primitive Hammer. The finished Copper Plate replaces the ingot visibly on the anvil; use an empty hand to take it.

$(bold)2. Mechanical Power$()$(br2)Copper Plates reinforce your first wooden mechanical components. Shafts carry rotation along their axis, while gears move rotation between parallel axes.$(br2)The current wooden gears have 8 and 16 teeth. Changing gear size changes speed and torque rather than creating free power.

pages.title: Shafts & Medium Gears
pages.text: Shafts form the backbone of a mechanical line. Medium gears are the smaller 8-tooth gear.

pages.title: Large Gears & Handle
pages.text: The handled Large Gear is your first mechanical power source. Right-click it to crank the network for a limited time. Ordinary gears are passive transmission components.

$(bold)Manual Mechanical Era$()$(br2)Early Copper Age machinery is intentionally hand-powered. The handled gear only drives the network for a limited time.$(br2)Build with shafts and gears now; later, continuous mechanical power should feel like a major upgrade rather than just another recipe.

pages.title: Mechanical Grinder
pages.text: The first powered machine is a simple two-block grinder: place the Mechanical Grinder Base and put the Grinder Stone directly above it, then right-click the base to form the multiblock.

pages.name: Mechanical Grinder
pages.text: The Grinder Stone sits directly above the base. Mechanical input is on the LEFT side of the upper grinding assembly. Place a Wooden Shaft beside that upper block, aligned horizontally into the visible wooden bearing. The grinder requires at least 20 mechanical speed and 4 torque.

$(bold)3. Crush the ore$()$(br2)Right-click the formed grinder with Chalcocite Ore to load it. Connect a powered Wooden Shaft to the visible bearing on the left side of the upper grinding assembly. With at least 20 speed and 4 torque, the grinder runs for about eight seconds and produces Crushed Chalcocite.$(br2)If the crank stops, processing pauses instead of losing progress. Use an empty hand on the grinder to retrieve its output.

$(bold)Why bother?$()$(br2)Direct Primitive Furnace processing remains valid: one Chalcocite Ore produces one Copper Ingot and Slag.$(br2)Crushing the Chalcocite first improves the same furnace batch to $(bold)two Copper Ingots$() plus Slag. Mechanical processing makes your ore more valuable instead of existing only as a progression lock.

$(bold)Next milestone: continuous power$()$(br2)The grinder is currently the first real consumer of the Gear V2 network. The next Copper Age milestone will replace repeated hand cranking with a continuous mechanical source.$(br2)The planned direction is a Water Wheel, followed by a larger mechanical workshop and additional processing.

$(bold)Later Copper Age$()$(br2)After continuous power, the age is planned to expand into improved Copper metallurgy, basic item logistics, and a small functioning mechanical factory rather than a checklist of machines.

$(bold)The road to Bronze$()$(br2)Cassiterite and Tin will form the final Copper Age challenge. Tin processing is intended to depend on the mechanical infrastructure learned during this age.$(br2)Combining processed Tin with Copper to produce the first Bronze will eventually mark the transition into the Bronze Age.
